svg.title: Four visits, two cancelling pairs
svg.desc: Two selected outward-offset fourfold meetings, one on 11 / 6 at distance about 57.58865 and one on 11 / 8 at about 110.66889. Four original visits touch a circle centered on the mirror axis. Offsetting by its radius brings all four to one point. Small local normal shifts with coefficients zero, one, three, and seven separate four ordinary triple events, two positive and two negative, at the distinct first-order weights shown on the right. Whole-orbit rational covers exclude a fifth branch. Pictures and horizontal positions are numerical illustrations of separate rational certificates, not a census of the full offset families.

g.text: A small break of the mirror separates four triple passages. Their signed changes cancel.
Four original visits · equal coordinate scales
Horizontal position: d in M = M* + εd + O(ε²)
Two positive and two negative triples · net change zero
Each row names three visits and their strangeness jump.

Selected higher meetings strengthen the outward lower bounds to 106 and 116 triple passages.
The sufficiently distant constructed route therefore needs at least 944 triples. Its exact leg counts remain open.
